summary: P. Perumal is an Indology and history/archaeology scholar who earned an M.L.I.Sc from Madurai Kamaraj University in 1985. In 1980, he served as a part-time conservator at the Saraswathi Mahal Library.

P. Pratap Kumar is a religious studies and Indology scholar. He served as a professor at the University of Durban-Westville (attested 2000-2001) and the University of KwaZulu-Natal (attested 2010), and as a visiting professor at Colorado College (attested 2010).

P. R. Subramanian works in Indology and linguistics. He was a lecturer at the University of Cologne (1972-1983), a visiting scholar at the Nordic Institute of Asian Studies, and affiliated with Mozhi Trust (attested 2019). He taught Asko Parpola.
P. S. Chandrasekharan is an Indologist who was a Ph.D. scholar at the Kuppuswami Sastri Research Institute under doctoral supervisor V. Yamuna Devi (attested 2026).
P. S. Joshi, a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology, served as principal of New English School, Ramanbag, and as Professor of Sanskrit at Fergusson College. He taught Thanon Chitkament.

Indologist and linguist P. S. Subrahmanya Sastri studied at Bishop Heber College, IASE Saidapet, and the University of Madras (Ph.D.). He held posts at Bishop Heber College, University of Madras, Rajah's College (Principal), and Annamalai University (Department Head).

P. Swaminathan is an Indologist who completed an M.Litt. at the University of Madras by 1956, supervised for his MA by V. Raghavan. He was a lecturer in Sanskrit at National Sanskrit University (attested 1965).
P. T. Narasimhachar was an Indology scholar who studied at Maharaja's College, Mysore, around 1923-1926 under Mysore Hiriyanna.
P. V. Ramanujaswami was an Indologist who served as Director of the Sri Venkateswara Oriental Research Institute, attested in 1944 and 1954.

Padma Subrahmanyam is a scholar in Indology and history/archaeology. She studied at Stella Maris College, Ethiraj College for Women, and Annamalai University (~1974-1979) under research supervisor T. N. Ramachandran.

Padmanabh S. Jaini studied at Mumbai, Vidyodaya Pirivena, and SOAS under John Brough. A Buddhist studies and Indology scholar, he was a professor at the University of Michigan (~1967-1972) and the University of California, Berkeley (~1972-1994).
Pagorn Singsuriya, a scholar in Buddhist studies and philosophy, studied at Chulalongkorn University and held an appointment in Humanities at Mahidol University (attested 2021).

Palden Gyal, a scholar of Tibetology, philosophy, and Buddhist studies, earned degrees from Duke, Harvard, and Columbia. Attested in 2026, he held a postdoctoral fellowship at the Heyman Center for the Humanities at Columbia University.

Pallabi Bagchi, active in history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies, earned a BA from Jadavpur University and a Ph.D. from Maharaja Sayajirao University of Baroda (2021-2025), where she was also a teaching assistant (2022-2025).
Palmer Boyd was an Indologist who studied at Trinity College (1867-1871, B.A.) under Edward Byles Cowell. He also held a post at Trinity College, Cambridge.

Palmira Brummett is a historian who studied at the University of Chicago and the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign. She was a professor emeritus at the University of Tennessee, Knoxville (~1989-2011) and a visiting professor at Brown University (2011-2016).
Palmo Kyi is a Tibetology scholar who studied under teachers Hanna Havnevik and Rinzin Thargyal, as well as supervisor Per Kværne (attested 2012).

Pamela D. Winfield works in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Japanology. She was affiliated with Temple University (attested 2001) and served as Associate Professor of Religious Studies at Elon University (attested 2015-2017).

Pamela Gutman was a scholar of history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Indology. She studied at the University of Vienna and was a research student at the Australian National University (~1972-1976).

Panahaduwe Yasassi is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He was Professor in Buddhist Civilization at the University of Sri Jayewardenepura (2020) and a professor at the Postgraduate Institute of Pali and Buddhist Studies (attested 2026).
